thesisQuality.note: Strong orders, revenue, cash and installed-base/aftermarket demand support durable aerospace value capture; margin/integration risk keeps below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 orders +17%, revenue +21%, adjusted operating profit +18%, FCF +43% and raised guidance support the strong anchor.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current market data shows roughly $331B market cap and ~37.6x trailing P/E, a demanding valuation versus otherwise strong growth.

catalystScore.note: CPP capacity acquisition and continued delivery/aftermarket conversion are material catalysts, but closing/integration remain forward-looking.

governancePower.note: Raised guidance and strong cash conversion support execution; $11.75B CPP purchase creates material capital-allocation/integration uncertainty.

alignment2036.note: Commercial aviation, defense propulsion and mission-critical engine capacity are durable infrastructure needs across multiple futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Commercial engines, aftermarket and defense reuse propulsion/casting capabilities across independent demand engines.

bottleneckControl.note: CPP explicitly expands ownership of mission-critical precision-casting capacity, a known engine-throughput constraint.

scenarioRobustness.note: Commercial, aftermarket and defense demand diversify outcomes, though aerospace-cycle and integration exposure remain.

substitutionResilience.note: Qualified engine platforms, installed-base aftermarket and mission-critical castings imply substantial replacement/qualification friction.

supplyChainResilience.note: CPP is a direct resilience action, but acquired capacity has not yet proven post-close throughput and qualification benefits.

pricingPower.note: Strong operating profit and cash growth amid inflation/mix pressure indicate some value capture, but margin contraction limits a higher anchor.

risk.note: Large CPP purchase creates integration/return risk; Q2 margin pressure shows growth is not frictionless.

confidence.note: Identity validated; two distinct issuer-primary origins plus independent current valuation; forward synergy economics remain unknown.

thesis: GE Aerospace combines strong propulsion demand and aftermarket cash generation with direct control of a casting bottleneck.
keyRisk: CPP integration/capital allocation and persistent margin pressure can dilute otherwise strong demand conversion.
nextCatalyst: CPP closing/integration milestones and October 2026 earnings/delivery update.
